## Transferable mechanism summary
Seed mechanism (usbip_recv_iso, demonstration only, never reportable): (1) Untrusted source: a peer-controlled count (urb->number_of_packets) copied verbatim from a remote protocol message (ret_submit unpack) into a shared kernel object before any validation — the attacker is the remote endpoint of a device/virtual-bus protocol, not a local user. (2) Missing guarantee: no bounds clamp of the count against the protocol maximum (USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS existed but was only enforced on the submit/other-direction path — asymmetric validation), and no overflow-checked sizing (manual `int size = np * sizeof(*iso)` in 32-bit instead of kcalloc/array_size/struct_size). (3) Unsafe use/state transition: the truncated product goes to kzalloc, then a per-element loop runs np iterations of recv+copy into the undersized heap buffer; additionally, the early-error return leaves the poisoned count set in urb->number_of_packets, which the URB completion path (processcompl) later iterates. (4) Consequence: remotely triggerable kernel heap buffer overflow (OOB write) plus OOB read on the completion/error-unwind path — memory corruption, crash/DoS, potential privilege escalation. Transferable invariant: whenever a length/count/size quantity crosses a trust boundary into kernel state, three guarantees must hold — the count is range-checked at parse time against a known maximum, every buffer-size computation derived from it is overflow-checked, and no failure path leaves the unchecked count in shared state for later iteration. BRANCHES: branch1=alloc-multiply-overflow (32-bit count*element-size or count+offset/shift arithmetic assigned to int/uint and passed to kmalloc/kzalloc/vmalloc/memdup followed by an element-indexed copy/recv loop, where the multiplier is untrusted — hunt the arithmetic-to-allocator-to-loop chain in driver and fs code within one snapshot); branch2=unclamped-wire-count (deserialization/unpack/recvmsg/netlink-nla/ioctl-in paths that copy count/length/nr_fields from the wire or userspace into kernel objects with no range check, especially where a sibling path of the same protocol enforces a MAX limit but the mirror path does not — asymmetric validation between paired directions); branch3=error-unwind-poisoned-count (early-return/failure/teardown paths that leave an attacker-controlled count/length/actual_size field set in a shared object — urb, request, skb, sgl, iovec — that a completion handler, cleanup routine, or status-out path later iterates, causing OOB access during error handling); branch4=peer-trusted-transport (kernel-side clients/servers of remote or virtual device transports — network-exported bus, virtual HCD, guest-host, remote-storage/remote-fs reply handlers — that allocate or loop based on peer-supplied response fields without cross-checking locally-known limits, i.e., trust-boundary consumption of a remote peer's reply, identified by mechanism rather than subsystem name); seed names (usbip, recv_iso, number_of_packets) must never be used as the finding itself.

## Current intent
Intent id: i057
Assigned snapshot: s02
Assigned branch: hci-completed-length-trust
SNAPSHOT=s02; BRANCH=hci-completed-length-trust; Search only snapshots/s02. New mechanism branch surfaced by facts f002 and f042, genuinely distinct from the four planned branches (parse-time wire counts, allocation arithmetic, error-unwind poisoned counts, peer-transport reply fields): completion-time transfer metadata — urb->actual_length and analogues such as SCSI/DMA request actual/residual (resid) counts and controller-set completion lengths, written by hardware or device firmware at completion time — consumed by completion handlers as a copy length, subtraction operand, or iteration bound without cross-check against the locally requested size such as transfer_buffer_length or the expected byte count. Known shapes from sibling audits to verify in this tree's exact state if present: drivers/usb/serial/opticon.c:76 'size_t data_len = urb->actual_length - 2;' (size_t underflow when a short or malicious completion reports actual_length < 2), drivers/usb/serial/kl5kusb105.c:360 'len = urb->actual_length - KLSI_HDR_LEN;', and the greybus es2.c bulk-in completion handing urb->actual_length into greybus_data_rcvd/gb_connection_recv whose memcpy destination is sized from local request state. Then sweep the other URB/request completion handlers in this one snapshot that use actual_length/actual/resid/byte_count as copy, loop, or subtraction operands (usb serial/core/misc/media/net/input, scsi resid paths, greybus/serdev, tty receive). Scope strictly to metadata the hardware/controller writes at completion time; parse-time wire counts, allocator arithmetic, and error-path leftover counts are covered by other branch intents on this snapshot and must not be re-reported here. For each candidate record file:line of the completion callback, the metadata field, the missing bound check, and the consuming copy/loop; a negative result must cite the completion handlers examined. The seed usbip path itself is demonstration-only and must never be reported as the finding; if unpatched usbip code is present, record it as excluded-by-rule and keep searching. {
  "hexsha": "1897852293faca4c2be51e0a19f739622f771623",
  "one_line_summary": "usb: usbip: fix integer overflow in usbip_recv_iso()",
  "vulnerability_summary": "Wire-controlled urb->number_of_packets multiplied by descriptor size in a 32-bit int overflows, causing a small kzalloc but a large receive loop write, yielding heap buffer overflow.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Wire-controlled count multiplied by fixed element size in narrow integer type overflows, producing undersized allocation followed by loop-based writes exceeding the buffer.",
  "patch": "commit 1897852293faca4c2be51e0a19f739622f771623
Author: Kelvin Mbogo <addcontent08@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Mar 25 13:36:38 2026 +0300

    usb: usbip: fix integer overflow in usbip_recv_iso()
    
    usbip_recv_iso() computes the iso descriptor buffer size as:
    
        int size = np * sizeof(*iso);
    
    where np comes straight from the wire (urb->number_of_packets, set by
    usbip_pack_ret_submit() before we get here).  With np = 0x10000001 and
    sizeof(*iso) == 16 the product is 0x100000010 which truncates to 16 on
    a 32-bit int.  kzalloc(16) succeeds but the following receive loop
    writes np * 16 bytes into it - game over.
    
    USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS (1024) already exists in usbip_common.h for the
    submit path but was never enforced on the receive side.
    
    Clamp np to [1, USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS] and switch to kcalloc() so
    the allocator itself can catch overflows in the future.  Fold the
    existing np == 0 early return into the new bounds check.
    
    usbip_pack_ret_submit() already copied the bogus np into
    urb->number_of_packets before we run, so just returning -EPROTO is
    not enough - processcompl() in the HCD will still iterate that many
    iso_frame_desc entries when it completes the failed URB.  Zero out
    urb->number_of_packets before bailing to prevent that secondary crash
    (confirmed on 6.12.0, processcompl+0x63 with CR2 in unmapped slab).
    
    Signed-off-by: Kelvin Mbogo <addcontent08@gmail.com>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260325103640.8090-1-addcontent08@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c b/drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c
index a2b2da1255dd..8b6eb7476747 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c
@@ -662,7 +662,7 @@ int usbip_recv_iso(struct usbip_device *ud, struct urb *urb)
 	void *buff;
 	struct usbip_iso_packet_descriptor *iso;
 	int np = urb->number_of_packets;
-	int size = np * sizeof(*iso);
+	int size;
 	int i;
 	int ret;
 	int total_length = 0;
@@ -670,11 +670,21 @@ int usbip_recv_iso(struct usbip_device *ud, struct urb *urb)
 	if (!usb_pipeisoc(urb->pipe))
 		return 0;
 
-	/* my Bluetooth dongle gets ISO URBs which are np = 0 */
-	if (np == 0)
-		return 0;
+	if (np <= 0 || np > USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS) {
+		dev_err(&urb->dev->dev,
+			"recv iso: invalid number_of_packets %d\n", np);
+		/*
+		 * usbip_pack_ret_submit() already set urb->number_of_packets
+		 * from the wire.  Zero it so processcompl() does not iterate
+		 * OOB descriptors on the way out.
+		 */
+		urb->number_of_packets = 0;
+		return -EPROTO;
+	}
+
+	size = np * sizeof(*iso);
 
-	buff = kzalloc(size, GFP_KERNEL);
+	buff = kcalloc(np, sizeof(*iso), GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!buff)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
"
}

    usb: usbip: fix integer overflow in usbip_recv_iso()
    
    usbip_recv_iso() computes the iso descriptor buffer size as:
    
        int size = np * sizeof(*iso);
    
    where np comes straight from the wire (urb->number_of_packets, set by
    usbip_pack_ret_submit() before we get here).  With np = 0x10000001 and
    sizeof(*iso) == 16 the product is 0x100000010 which truncates to 16 on
    a 32-bit int.  kzalloc(16) succeeds but the following receive loop
    writes np * 16 bytes into it - game over.
    
    USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS (1024) already exists in usbip_common.h for the
    submit path but was never enforced on the receive side.
    
    Clamp np to [1, USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS] and switch to kcalloc() so
    the allocator itself can catch overflows in the future.  Fold the
    existing np == 0 early return into the new bounds check.
    
    usbip_pack_ret_submit() already copied the bogus np into
    urb->number_of_packets before we run, so just returning -EPROTO is
    not enough - processcompl() in the HCD will still iterate that many
    iso_frame_desc entries when it completes the failed URB.  Zero out
    urb->number_of_packets before bailing to prevent that secondary crash
    (confirmed on 6.12.0, processcompl+0x63 with CR2 in unmapped slab).
